item: Airplane mode refuses a plain http:// fetch through a loopback HTTP proxy before a byte reaches the proxy
summary: R619, from Steward 3's second security read of R616. A plain http:// URL fetched through an HTTP proxy (Privoxy chained to Tor, settings http_proxy) is written by urllib3 and by urllib.request as an absolute-form request line, GET http://host/x, to the loopback proxy socket, with no CONNECT. The socket guard saw only the allowed loopback connect and _tunnel is never called, so in airplane mode the proxy received the whole request and could forward it; live-reproduced with a loopback listener before the fix. src/ingest/airplane.py now also patches http.client.HTTPConnection.putrequest, the one call every http.client-based client hands its request target to before writing anything (urllib3 reaches it through super()), and, while airplane mode is on, refuses every request target that names its own destination: anything but origin-form /path (never //), exactly * or empty, so absolute-form and CONNECT (method compared after strip) included, whatever host it names. A loopback name is not exempt, because a forwarding proxy chained upstream (Privoxy forward-socks5t) forwards localhost like any other name, and the first version's host parse failed open on http://127.0.0.1?@evil.com/, %25 and [::1]evil.com (Opus read) and missed //host, host:80, http:/host and CONNECT-with-a-space (second security read). The refusal names no part of the target (R142). The new point joins _patch_points, the heal check, uninstall and the conftest leak check. Tests: a loopback listener receives zero bytes from requests and from urllib.request in airplane mode, receives the absolute-form GET online (the control), and receives it again with the putrequest patch removed (remove the guard, a test fails); loopback-looking targets through urllib leave zero bytes too; unit cases for every shape both reads found; no_proxy cleared so the tests cannot go direct. SECURITY.md also states that the connect-time SSRF guard cannot see a proxied destination. Stated limit: httpx/httpcore does not use http.client, so this patch point does not cover it; in this tree httpx is used only by the loopback-only LLM clients. Not touched: the https-through-a-loopback-proxy labelling issue (Export lane). Release-notes line: with airplane mode on, a fetch sent through a local HTTP proxy is now refused before any byte reaches the proxy, whatever address it names.
